newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Govt and Khmer Rouge hardliners vie for camp.
newsitem.headline: Govt and Khmer Rouge hardliners vie for camp.

text.p: Government soldiers and Khmer Rouge dissidents are battling hardline Khmer Rouge guerrillas for control of a village in northwest Cambodia, military and provincial officials said on Friday.

"We are still clashing with the Khmer Rouge hardliners," said Lieutenant General Nhek Bun Chhay, the armed forces deputy chief of staff. He said the guerrillas controlled only half of Chup Koki village on the northwestern border with Thailand.
The general had no figure for casualties.

Hem Bunheng, deputy governor of Siem Reap province, said the government had sent 200 soldiers to help the dissident fighters recapture Chup Koki, the first village taken by Pol Pot loyalists since the Maoist group split in early August.
Thai and Cambodia officials had said the village fell after a 20-minute clash on Wednesday. The fighting sent hundreds of villagers fleeing into Thailand.
The breakaway faction is negotiating a peace deal with Phnom Penh. It is led by Ieng Sary, the foreign minister during the Khmer Rouge's reign of terror under Pol Pot in the 1970s.
More than one million Cambodians died from execution, starvation, disease or overwork during the Khmer Rouge rule, which began in April 1975 and lasted more than three years.

Sporadic fighting between the Khmer Rouge dissidents and Pol Pot's faction began shortly after Ieng Sary announced the break and formed a new organisation called the Democratic National United Movement.
The Khmer Rouge guerrillas signed a U.N.-brokered peace pact for Cambodia in 1991 but reneged on the accord. They have since been fighting the coalition that emerged from general elections in 1993.
